newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs slide on rate, supply concerns.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs slide on rate, supply concerns.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures came under intense pressure on Wednesday on fears of stronger than expected economic data and excess supply in the bond market.

Dealers said JGB futures were sold off and dragged Euroyen down with them on news that Standard and Poor's had assigned a Bpi rating to three Japanese life insurers, raising fears the companies might sell JGBs.
June JGBs ended at 122.60, just above their intraday low, against a previous 123.29.
December Euroyen was quoted at 98.77 at 1120 GMT after falling as low as 98.75 against an IMM close at 98.86. Volume was an active 39,015 lots.
A trader at an Asian institution said stop-loss sales were triggered around the 98.85 and 98.80 levels.
Despite some short-covering towards the close, he said the contract was likely to head lower and test 98.72 on Thursday. June JGBs were seen targetting 122.06.
Rumours Japan's April industrial production data, due on Thursday, would be better than expected also placed pressure on the Japanese interest rate futures market, he said.
A Japanese futures house dealer said forecasts for the industrial output data ranged between rises of 0.1 percent and 2.5 percent.
"This number tends to be quite wild so it's not worth betting on it," he said.
Dealers said news the Bank of Japan would release its quarterly business sentiment survey, or tankan, on June 25 instead of in early July as previously announced, also depressed the market.
The Japanese central bank said the earlier release of the tankan did not indicate any change in its monetary policy.
Eurodollar futures slipped on follow-through selling after a weak overnight close in Chicago and ahead of the release of the U.S. durable goods report for April at 1230 GMT.
December Eurodollars ended at 93.660 against their IMM close at 93.680 on volume of 11,625 lots.
